title: Structured Invocation Manifest and Error Advisor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Proposal: introduce a compact "Invocation Manifest" JSON format to standardize tool/function call schemas across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, plus a runtime "Error Advisor" that surfaces human-friendly diagnostics and automated repair suggestions. Goal is to reduce unexpected runtime failures from schema drift, ambiguous unions, and streaming/tool-handshake edge cases while preserving backward compatibility and minimal payload overhead. The manifest emphasizes: 1) concise type hints (string/int/float/boolean/object/array), 2) coercion profiles (strict|permissive|hinted), 3) example vectors for common inputs, 4) canonical error codes with remediation hints, and 5) telemetry keys to correlate validation failures with request traces. This ticket covers schema design, runtime validation rules, error mapping, and diagnostic UX contract for the Console and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Define Invocation Manifest JSON grammar and publish spec doc link
Runtime validates manifest-specified params with clear error codes at call-time
Error Advisor produces human-friendly message and a single actionable remediation hint for each error code
SDK shows same diagnostic strings and exposes a repair_hint field in call-failure responses
Telemetry events emitted for validation failures with <error_code, model, route, region> tags
Backward-compatibility shim accepts legacy function-call shapes and emits deprecation telemetry
design_notes: Key decisions: 1) format is intentionally compact - keys are single words (name, type, required, mode, example, doc_hint); 2) coercion modes defined so runtime can attempt safe fixes for permissive manifests but never mutate values in strict manifests; 3) error advisor returns 'repair_hint' with a short checklist and a 'confidence' label (low|medium|high); 4) streaming calls will include a 'stream_handshake' block in the manifest describing partial-output expectations and finalization token. We avoid embedding full JSON Schema due to payload size and parsing cost; we'll provide a transform tool that expands Invocation Manifest to a full JSON Schema when needed for offline tooling and docs.
telemetry_schema_notes: Each event must include keys: error_code, route, model_id, region, manifest_version, invocation_id, latency_ms
error_code_catalog: INV-001: missing_required - required parameter missing. repair_hint: 'Provide parameter <name> or mark it optional in manifest.'
INV-002: type_mismatch - parameter type incompatible. repair_hint: 'Convert value to <expected_type> or update manifest coercion mode to permissive for this param.'
INV-003: coercion_failed - runtime attempted coercion but failed. repair_hint: 'Review example values for this param; consider adding parsing guidance or stricter client validation.'
INV-004: extraneous_field - unexpected field present. repair_hint: 'Remove unknown field or update manifest to include a catch_all/extra flag.'
INV-005: ambiguous_union - union types matched multiple branches. repair_hint: 'Disambiguate union by adding discriminator or constraining examples.'

INV-006: streaming_finalizer_mismatch - streaming call did not emit expected finalization token. repair_hint: 'Ensure agent sends final token described by stream_handshake.final_token or set finalization_timeout.'
INV-007: nested_depth_exceeded - input nested object depth exceeds manifest max_depth. repair_hint: 'Flatten structure or increase manifest max_depth with caution.'
INV-008: array_element_type_variance - array contains mixed element types when manifest expects uniform type. repair_hint: 'Normalize array elements or declare union element type in manifest.'
validation_playbook: Runtime validator behavior: - For strict params: fail fast with INV-001/INV-002 and do not attempt coercion. - For permissive params: attempt JSON-native coercions (string->number, number->string) and if successful emit invocations.validation.repair_attempt telemetry; if coercion fails emit INV-003. - For hinted params: provide repair_hint in diagnostics but allow call to proceed with best-effort coercion. For streaming calls, validator checks handshake at start and validates finalizer token at end; missing or mismatched finalizer raises INV-006.
examples: manifest minimal example: {name: 'user_age', type: 'int', required: true, mode: 'strict', example: 29}
manifest permissive example: {name: 'quantity', type: 'int', required: false, mode: 'permissive', example: '3'}
backwards_compatibility_strategy: Support legacy call shapes by running legacy_adaptor which maps legacy payloads to Invocation Manifest during intake. When adaptor performs non-trivial mapping, emit invocation.manifest.deprecation with mapping_type and suggest client migration paths. Provide an opt-in feature flag 'manifest_strict_mode' on Dedicated & Private for early adopters.
testing_plan: Unit tests for validator coercion paths, fuzz tests for union and ambiguous cases, integration tests for streaming handshake, end-to-end runs against SDKs with sample manifests. Create synthetic workloads to exercise deprecation path. Performance tests to ensure validation adds <2ms median latency on hot path.
rollout_plan: 1) merge runtime PR behind runtime.flag.invocation_manifest 2) enable for 5% of hosted traffic with manifest_strict_mode=false 3) monitor telemetry for INV-* rates and repair_attempt ratios 4) increase to 25% then 100% after 2 weeks of stability, 5) flip manifest_strict_mode for selected enterprise tenants in Dedicated. Console will surface top-10 failing schemas and suggested edits.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: new validation could surface a spike in failures for older clients. Mitigation: start permissive for hosted, expose repair_hint to SDKs, ship migration guide and opt-out. Risk: extra CPU in runtime. Mitigation: cache compiled manifests and use vectorized validator in C++ path.
open_questions: What is the canonical manifest versioning strategy and how do we surface breaking changes?
Should the Error Advisor expose machine-actionable patches (e.g., small JSON patch) or only human hints?
Do we allow manifest-embedded regexes for string validation or disallow due to CPU complexity?
